title: J. I. de Swart (St Petersburg) to P. van Bleiswijk, 8 March 1782, Nationaal Archief 3.01.25 inv. 610 (DECODE R1036)

steps.what: Fetched R1036, R1040 and R1038 scans and DECODE transcriptions, plus sibling pairs R2045, R2195, R2032, R2051 and R2052.
Leeuw 2000 and the Oterleek-codes paper (HistoCrypt 2026) identified the Croiset codebook family and the two-codebook 1787 letter. No prior decipherment was found.
Parsed DECODE's R1038 key transcription to 5,961 entries, keeping the digit marks as part of the group.
Tried the 1803 Croiset relative on R1036/R1040. The apparent hits gave nonsense.
Applied the key to R1036: 1,448 of 1,719 groups (84.2%). Then 25 values from repeated contexts (Spa+nje, Dene+mar+ken, lijk, ing[en]) brought it to 91.9%.
Located the codebook switch in R1040 at group 180 of image 5459 and read the second segment with the 1765 key at 84-90% a page.
Aligned the 1784-86 plain/cipher pairs R2032, R2051 and R2052 to rebuild the missing first key of R1040. The transfers cover 2-3% and give no prose.

Nine more contextual values, each consistent at every occurrence: 741=haar (12x), 39=hun, 2=een, 176^^=mpli (pure et simpliciter), 410^_=zij, 681^_=mogendheden, 724=welgeval, 3^o=stel, 363^o=tusschen. R1036 now at 1,613/1,719 (93.8%).

Read 50 key entries that DECODE's R1038 transcription left illegible or mislabelled directly from the codebook scans (the word stands to the left of its code; parallel homophone columns confirm faint words). 41 were kept after checking them against the R1036 contexts (e.g. 781=geheel, 748''=commercie, 488_=Zijne Keizerlijke Majesteit, 515o=twaalf, 640 barred circle=Russisch). R1036 now at 1,663/1,719 (96.7%). The rest are low-confidence, shadowed or blank in the scans.

Greek-project passage checked group by group against the codebook scans: three earlier scan readings had taken the word to the right of the code (54'' is alhoewel, not alle; 314'' behalven; 941_ observeeren, not obtineeren); 47_ is k, not DECODE's l (gives Griekse and Denemarken); 327=el, 92_=houden, 121=die, 862^^=het, 448''=con fixed by alphabetical place; 644_ reads 'Veld Ma..' (rest in the binding shadow), 339_ faint ('man'?). Not yet applied to decode_1765.py.

Letter images 5416-5417 checked: the '^_' DECODE writes before some groups is a dash after the previous group, so 380 there is plain 380 = van (four DECODE 'krijgen?') and 303 = die (not koop); 21 tokens take their only mark from that dash. The group after 362_ (jong) is an interlinear 191 = ens (DECODE: 19). The first line of image 5417 is cut off in the photograph, losing the end of the Greek sentence.

Normalised Dutch reading of the Emperor/Greek-project passage (tokens 239-466, 686-775) with English, graded M/I: Constantine in the hands of a Greek woman and taught Greek, orders to Field Marshal Ru[man]zow (probably Rumyantsev, unverified) for twelve Greek boys; the Empress silent even to her confidants but the project not dropped. Open: 231o, 77o, 738, 299, 553's role, [dan] (601 with a bar, komen: probably an encoding slip), the lost line.

Greek-project passage: open groups read from their place in the R1038 codebook scans: 738 = grond (M), 299 = favoriet (I), 231^o = verder (I); 77^o ('Stans' in the book) and the line cut off on image 5417 still open.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: DECODE said the codebook could not be identified; the 1765 Croiset codebook of the Russia legation (DECODE R1038, a separate key record) was found here to fit and read 84% of R1036 as transcribed on DECODE; 34 values from context and 41 entries read directly from the R1038 scans raised it to 96.7%.
outcome.notes: R1036 read; 56 groups (51 distinct rare codes) are open, mostly entries lost in the scan's binding shadow. R1040 read in part: the second segment only; the first needs the missing Rechteren key (NA inv. 158, not online).

credits.note: Croiset's 1765 codebook of the Russia legation (DECODE R1038), read from its scans
DECODE transcriptions of R1036 and of the R1038 key

prior.where: No published decipherment of R1036 or R1040 was found; the key R1038 is on DECODE

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.
